title: Prototypicality Bias Reveals Blindspots in Multimodal Evaluation Metrics

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating whether multimodal metrics systematically prefer visually and socially typical (prototypical) images that contain explicit semantic errors over semantically correct but non-prototypical images using a controlled contrastive benchmark (PROTOBIAS).

Measuring whether metrics incorrectly prefer stereotypical depictions of religious groups (pairing Christian vs. Muslim/Jewish identities with positive or negative socio-attributes) over counter-stereotypical depictions, despite the stereotypical images containing explicit semantic violations.

Measuring whether metrics incorrectly prefer stereotypical depictions of nationalities (pairing American vs. Nigerian, Indian, or Mexican identities with specific socio-attributes) over counter-stereotypical depictions, despite the stereotypical images containing explicit semantic violations.

Measuring whether metrics incorrectly prefer stereotypical depictions of sexual orientations (pairing heterosexual vs. LGBTQ+ identities with specific socio-attributes) over counter-stereotypical depictions, despite the stereotypical images containing explicit semantic violations.
